facts.text: McCune was founded by Isaac McCune in 1878, when a post office moved from the nearby town of Time and the new settlement was named after him.
The town was laid out in May 1879, with the Louis–San Francisco Railroad’s Parsons subdivision surveying and platting the streets.
McCune sits on a natural divide between the Neosho River and Lightning Creek, giving the area exceptionally fertile, well‑drained soils ideal for farming.
The town’s first post office, established in August 1878, was part of an international money‑order system that served six rural routes.
